c4af93d2613324e770baa61db1e1141081b8074b: Col de Rousset is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 22 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Col de Rousset's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Col de Rousset's modest altitude, starting at 1255 m and topping out at 1700 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before setting off is strongly advised. With a day lift pass at just 18€, Col de Rousset is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget, or skiers who want to fit in plenty of days without breaking the bank, it is a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: Col de Rousset does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

c4c804c02c73c116f4200bfb48d3aaa88dd32bb2: A resort on a human scale, Garmisch-Partenkirchen focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 40 km of runs are well suited to a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Garmisch-Partenkirchen's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Garmisch-Partenkirchen's altitude (740 m at the base, 2,050 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow cover in the middle of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is wise to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Garmisch-Partenkirchen is clearly high: €69 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Garmisch-Partenkirchen does not compete with the giants of skiing and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underestimated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
